title: Normalized two-open tensor chains in both tensor orders
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Write $D_A(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-$A$ module sheaves. Use the actual pullback, derived tensor, signed symmetry $\sigma$, section-normalized adjunction units $\eta^i$, open base-change maps $\beta$, open tensor maps $\gamma$, and unique-left-adjoint open compositors of [def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations], with their normalization as in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] and the canonical tensor/pullback identifications of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. All complexes are arbitrary unbounded objects. Let $w:W\hookrightarrow V$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be open immersions, put $u=vw$, and let $F\in D_A(V)$, $H\in D_A(Y)$, $Q\in D_A(W)$ and $\delta:Lv^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}w_!Q$ be given. For every open $i:T\hookrightarrow S$, $K\in D_A(S)$ and $L\in D_A(T)$ define
$$\rho^i_{K,L}=i_!(\sigma_{L,Li^*K})\circ\gamma^i_{L,K}\circ\sigma_{K,i_!L}:K\otimes_A^Li_!L\longrightarrow i_!(Li^*K\otimes_A^LL).$$
This is an isomorphism whose restriction along $i$, under the stated units and tensor comparisons, is the identity on $Li^*K\otimes_A^LL$. The canonical compositor $c_{v,w}:v_!w_!\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!$ satisfies, under $Lu^*\cong Lw^*Lv^*$,
$$Lu^*(c_{v,w,L})\circ Lw^*(\eta^v_{w_!L})\circ\eta^w_L=\eta^u_L$$
for every $L\in D_A(W)$.

Define the two actual composites
$$e_L:v_!F\otimes_A^LH\xrightarrow{\gamma^v}v_!(F\otimes_A^LLv^*H)\xrightarrow{v_!(1\otimes\delta)}v_!(F\otimes_A^Lw_!Q)\xrightarrow{v_!(\rho^w)}v_!w_!(Lw^*F\otimes_A^LQ)\xrightarrow{c_{v,w}}u_!(Lw^*F\otimes_A^LQ),$$
$$e_R:H\otimes_A^Lv_!F\xrightarrow{\rho^v}v_!(Lv^*H\otimes_A^LF)\xrightarrow{v_!(\delta\otimes1)}v_!(w_!Q\otimes_A^LF)\xrightarrow{v_!(\gamma^w)}v_!w_!(Q\otimes_A^LLw^*F)\xrightarrow{c_{v,w}}u_!(Q\otimes_A^LLw^*F).$$
Put $T=Lw^*F$ and $d=(\eta^w_Q)^{-1}\circ Lw^*(\delta):Lw^*Lv^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$. Let $a:Lu^*v_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be $Lw^*((\eta^v_F)^{-1})$ under restriction composition. Define
$$r_L=(a\otimes d)\circ\mu_{u;v_!F,H},\qquad r_R=(d\otimes a)\circ\mu_{u;H,v_!F}.$$
Here the $d$ factors use $Lu^*H\cong Lw^*Lv^*H$. Both $e_L$ and $e_R$ are isomorphisms and their actual restrictions satisfy
$$Lu^*e_L=\eta^u_{T\otimes_A^LQ}\circ r_L,\qquad Lu^*e_R=\eta^u_{Q\otimes_A^LT}\circ r_R.$$
No boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor-amplitude is assumed.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-finite-open-gamma-restriction to the published gamma. By lem-pur-finite-tensor-pull-coherence pullback commutes with the signed symmetry, which is natural and involutive. Expand rho, move the inner symmetry past the open unit by naturality, then past the inverse-unit tensor map by symmetry naturality. The adjacent two symmetries cancel, giving the exact rho restriction formula. Gamma is an isomorphism from its published projection isomorphism; the involutive symmetry gives an explicit inverse, hence rho is an isomorphism.

For the actual compositor comp, apply Mathlib Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app to the composite adjunction transported along pullComp.symm. Expand ofNatIsoRight_unit and comp_unit_app. This gives exactly the first conjunct, including the inverse pullback compositor.

The private nestedRestriction calculation combines the two unit-normalized one-open maps: pullback-compositor naturality rewrites restriction along the composite as iterated restriction; naturality of the v-unit moves it past the inner map; substitute the inner normalization and the compositor-unit equation. This gives the composite unit after the product of the two restriction maps.

In the left chain put b=inverse eta-v at F and d=w-star(delta) followed by inverse eta-w at Q. Gamma normalization at v and rho normalization at w give the two inputs to nestedRestriction. Naturality of tensorPullIso moves tensor(1,delta) past the w comparison. Tensor-map functoriality combines its coordinates with inverse eta-w. Apply nestedTensorMap: tensor-comparison naturality and composition compatibility give the specified r_L. The right chain uses rho at v and gamma at w, giving r_R with the order Q tensor w-star F throughout. These are explicit equalities of the named maps, not support-based detection of equality.

Every factor is invertible: gamma by the actual published projection isomorphism, rho by the symmetry calculation, tensor(delta) by functoriality, and comp by adjunction uniqueness. Functors preserve isomorphisms, proving invertibility of both complete chains.

Step 2: σ compatibility from lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso plus η-naturality gives i^*ρ = η∘(1⊗η^{-1})∘μ, because the Koszul braiding is involutive. Step 3: the compositor-unit equation is exactly Mathlib unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (Adjunction/Unique.lean 51-55) for the composite adjunction of def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, with its right adjoint identified with u^* through pullComp, which is how def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations defines comp. Steps 4-6: I checked the arrow types of f_L and f_R, the use of naturality of η^v at f, naturality of μ_w in b, and the composition clause μ_u = μ_w∘w^*μ_v; this gives r_L and r_R, with the Q⊗T order kept in Step 6. Step 7: invertibility is correct. ℓ is invertible on the k-schemes since ℓ≠p, and every cited clause allows arbitrary unbounded inputs. I checked edge cases: identity opens, empty W, and signs for odd⊗odd factors. Duplicate search: only lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition is nearby, and it states invertibility and coherence but no unit equation. The proof is not circular and no source is SGA. lean.statement: theorem twoOpenTensorChainNormalization (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (W V Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k))) [IsSeparated W.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType W.hom] [QuasiCompact W.hom] [IsSeparated V.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType V.hom] [QuasiCompact V.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] (w : W ⟶ V) (v : V ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion w.left] [IsOpenImmersion v.left] (F : FiniteD P.Coefficient V.left) (H : FiniteD P.Coefficient Y.left) (Q : FiniteD P.Coefficient W.left) (δ : (pull P.Coefficient v.left).obj H ≅ (finiteShriek P.Coefficient w.left).obj Q) : (∀ L : FiniteD P.Coefficient W.left, (adj P.Coefficient w.left).unit.app L ≫ (pull P.Coefficient w.left).map ((adj P.Coefficient v.left).unit.app ((finiteShriek P.Coefficient w.left).obj L)) ≫ (pullComp P.Coefficient w.left v.left).inv.app ((finiteShriek P.Coefficient v.left).obj ((finiteShriek P.Coefficient w.left).obj L)) ≫ (pull P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).map ((comp P.Coefficient w.left v.left).hom.app L) = (adj P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).unit.app L) ∧ IsIso (twoOpenLeftChain P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ) ∧ IsIso (twoOpenRightChain P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ) ∧ ((pull P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).map (twoOpenLeftChain P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ) = twoOpenLeftRestriction P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ ≫ (adj P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).unit.app (tensor P.Coefficient W.left ((pull P.Coefficient w.left).obj F) Q)) ∧ ((pull P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).map (twoOpenRightChain P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ) = twoOpenRightRestriction P.Coefficient w.left v.left F H Q δ ≫ (adj P.Coefficient (w.left ≫ v.left)).unit.app (tensor P.Coefficient W.left Q ((pull P.Coefficient w.left).obj F)))
